subject: Budget range validation - NovaPay procurement thresholds
messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Budget range validation - NovaPay follow-up

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a couple of clarifying questions so we can get the right pricing band in the proposal:

- Usage profile you described: production chat for fraud ops + nightly batch reranks. You estimated peak months around 80–125M tokens and baseline months ~25–40M.
- Important procurement notes you mentioned: annual procurement thresholds (PO / legal review) and VP approvals for spend bands.

Can you confirm the following so we can model unit economics precisely:
1) Expected steady-state monthly token volume (range is fine).
2) Any internal target for $/1M tokens you’re trying to hit for procurement justification.
3) Procurement thresholds / approval gates (e.g., >$50k needs legal, >$150k needs VP sign-off).

I attached the usage_estimates.csv I sketched from the call (very rough). Once we have the volume band + target $/1M tokens I’ll share a clear hosted vs dedicated cost comparison and an initial commercial proposal.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three items above this week, I’ll follow up with pricing options and a recommended rollout (canary -> full).

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@novapay.com>

Cc: Karen Liu <karen.liu@novapay.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - NovaPay follow-up

Thanks Dylan — good summary. Confirming the items from our side:

1) Steady-state monthly token volume (range): 30M–90M tokens. We expect Q3 to be the high point (~120M) if a marketing push goes well, but normal months land in the 30–90M band.

2) Internal target $/1M tokens: we’re aiming for procurement justification around $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens. That’s the ballpark that keeps our monthly spend under the threshold for our business unit.

3) Procurement thresholds / approval gates:
   - < $50k annual: no special approvals.
   - $50k–$150k annual: procurement review + legal standard SOW (no exec sign-off).
   - $150k–$300k annual: requires VP approval and additional security questionnaire review.
   - > $300k annual: requires RFP process and exec procurement involvement.

For monthly framing, that roughly maps to: < $4k/mo, $4k–$12.5k/mo, $12.5k–$25k/mo, > $25k/mo respectively.

We’re happy to look at hosted API pricing first; if the unit economics look good we’ll consider a Dedicated reserved pool, but that triggers a separate procurement track.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow-up if it helps.

—Sam
Sam Peterson
Head of Data Products, NovaPay
sam.peterson@novapay.com

Attachment: procurement_thresholds.xlsx (procurement banding - stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - NovaPay follow-up

Thanks Sam — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications and what I’ll include in the proposal:

- We can target a hosted list price of $1,000 / 1M tokens for the baseline model family and provide volume tiers starting at 10% discount at 50M+ and up to 30% at 300M+. We’ll put together a blended tiered example so your finance team can see monthly impact.
- For the 30M–90M steady-state band, that maps to ~$30k–$90k / month at $1k/1M; with a 10% volume discount that becomes ~$27k–$81k. If Q3 hits 120M+ we’d recommend evaluating a Dedicated reserved profile where per-token economics improve and you get predictable throughput.
- Procurement thresholds you listed align with what we’ve seen. If the monthly spend starts trending toward the $12.5k–$25k band we should involve Rishi and our legal ops earlier.

Next steps: Marissa and Rishi — can you please prepare 2 commercial options:
  1) Hosted: tiered per-1M pricing with monthly spend examples mapped to NovaPay bands.
  2) Dedicated: reserve vs burst cost comparison and high-level timeline for procurement.

Sam — once Marissa shares the doc I’ll add a short note tying the monthly spend bands to procurement approval gates for your finance/procurement team.

Thanks,
Dylan
